links.targetTitle: Each Executive Sheet item carries three independent confirma

title: Content Liaisons cannot edit the Executive Sheet, so their confirmation is a comment that the Governance Point transcribes
content:
A.1.10.2.4.5.3 specifies an odd-looking two-step: "The Content Liaisons do not have access to edit the Executive Sheet, and therefore leave a comment in the document at the appropriate cell to provide confirmation. After the Content Liaisons confirm their items by leaving a comment, the Governance Point edits the Executive Sheet from 'Unconfirmed' to 'Confirmed'."

The indirection is a feature. The party attesting cannot alter the artifact they attest to, which means a Liaison cannot quietly adjust a value and then confirm the adjusted version. Write access stays with one accountable role while attestation is distributed to many — and each confirmation exists twice, as the Liaison's comment and as the Governance Point's status cell, so a discrepancy between them is detectable.

The comment is the actual provenance; A.1.10.2.4.5.1.5 classifies such Google Sheets comments as strong comment type provenance, which is why they must survive as a record rather than being replaced by the status flag.

One detail carries real weight: "the comments are only made for cells of the type 'Derived'." Liaisons confirm "addresses, token amounts, parameter values, etc." — the concrete, checkable specifics — not the high-level Input Action. Their attestation is a claim about facts within their competence, not endorsement of a policy, which keeps the sign-off narrow enough to be meaningful.
description: Attestation and record-keeping are split between parties, and comments attach only to Derived cells — confirmation binds concrete values like addresses and amounts, never high-level intent.
